milestones.name: The sea's waves are computed on the CPU alone, from glassy calm to gale, and agree with wave theory
milestones.quality_bar: An oracle a GPU can be held to: every result follows from wave theory or a closed form, as the reference evaluators in a shipped physics library do, and nothing in it needs a graphics device.

items.statement: From wind speed and direction, fetch and a list of swells, `thrum-sea-model` builds one spectrum split at 20 m: at most 192 long-wave components above the split and three cascade bands below it. No wave vector is in two layers, and the layers' variances sum to the spectrum's.
items.ask: Read the test. Is its tolerance on the summed variance derived from the quadrature it uses, and is it tighter than the smallest band's share? Does it cover a glassy calm, a trade wind and a gale, each with and without swell?

items.statement: Significant height rises with wind: under 5 cm with wind below 1 m/s and no swell, and 5 m or more for a fully developed sea at 20 m/s. Each long-wave component obeys the deep-water relation, frequency squared equals g times wavenumber.

The f64 long-wave evaluator gives, for a world point and a time, the height of the surface above that point, its slope, the surface's velocity and the time derivative of height. A one-component sea matches the closed form, and a point 20 km from the origin after 24 hours agrees with the same sum taken in extended precision to a micrometre.
items.ask: Does the closed-form comparison use values the test worked out without calling the evaluator? Does the test cover a sea steep enough that the surface above a point must be found by iteration, and say when the iteration cannot converge?

items.statement: A direct f64 sum over one cascade band's wave vectors and a 256-square inverse transform of the same band agree at every texel centre, for displacement, slopes and the Jacobian, to one part in a billion of the band's RMS height.

A change of wind or swell keeps every component's and every bin's phase and moves its power toward the new spectrum along the declared response curve. The model's height at a fixed point has no step at the change.

A conformance harness takes any provider of sea answers and reports its largest difference from the model in height, slope and velocity over a stated set of points and ticks. Given the model it reports zero; given the model with one component's phase moved, it reports the height that move makes.
`thrum-sea-model` builds and its tests run with no graphics device and no dependency on `thrum-render` or `wgpu`, and it holds no preset, hull or water table.
items.check: cargo tree --locked --offline -p thrum-sea-model -e normal | python3 -c 'import sys; t=sys.stdin.read(); sys.exit(1 if ("wgpu" in t or "thrum-render" in t or not t.strip()) else 0)'
items.ask: Does any file in the crate or its tests name a sea preset, a hull or a water type that belongs to a game?

items.statement: No file in this milestone is copied or translated from Broadsides unless the owner's licence for it is recorded in the log, and then `docs/evidence/SEA/PROVENANCE.md` lists the file with its source commit, path and licence.
items.ask: Does the provenance file exist and say either that nothing was lifted or which files were, and does the log hold the owner's licence if any were?

milestones.name: The GPU computes the same sea as the CPU model at every frame's time, after a day of running, through pauses, hitches and a replaced device
milestones.quality_bar: A sea that is the same waves at the same time however frames fall, as a shipped simulation's is, held to an independent oracle and not to its own earlier output.

items.statement: On Metal, for a gale 50 km from the origin after 24 hours of ticks, the long waves at 4,096 scattered points and at every field-cache texel centre match the CPU model within 2 mm in height. The largest difference in height and in slope is recorded.
items.ask: Is each field-cache level compared with the model restricted to the components that level holds, and are the scattered points evaluated by the kernel the body query will use?

items.statement: Each cascade's displacement and rate of change on Metal match the model's direct f64 sum at 1,024 texel centres, at a frame time between two ticks, within the first minute and after 24 hours. The largest difference is recorded as a share of the band's RMS height, and the test holds that one recorded bound at both times.
items.ask: Is the recorded difference under 1% of each band's RMS height, and was the bound written from a measurement on this Mac and in the record with its date and commit? Does the 24-hour case fail when the phase is formed from seconds in f32?

items.statement: Each cascade's mips hold the slope mean and covariance and the Jacobian's mean and variance, equal to the same moments computed from the base level.

Through a scripted run of frames between ticks, repeated ticks, a pause, a hitch of many ticks, a discarded frame, a capture frame at another tick, a backward tick, a new timeline and a replaced device, the long waves, the cascades and the field cache of every submitted frame are the model's sea at that frame's display time, and a capture frame's are the model's at the capture's own time. The sea keeps no ambient field from one frame for the next: a frame that follows a discarded frame or a replaced device is no different from any other.
items.ask: Are the expectations written from the model at each frame's time, and not from an earlier run of the GPU code? Do two frames on one tick with different interpolation alphas show different seas, and does a pause show one?

items.statement: During a wind change the GPU's sea follows the model's transition at every frame's time, with no step in height at fixed points.

The same tests pass on a Metal device held to WebGPU's default limits and to the storage formats and counts in the recorded Chrome capability record. A profile that exceeds a limit is refused at preparation, by name.
The GPU time of each sea simulate pass per frame, by pass name, and the bytes of every sea resource are on record for this Mac with the load on the machine, beside the design's estimates.

Each cascade bin in `thrum-sea-model` turns a whole number of times in the profile's loop, with a frequency within half a cycle per loop of the deep-water value, so the cascades at a time and one loop later are equal. The long waves keep the exact deep-water relation and do not repeat.

milestones.name: A float and a small craft ride the waves they sit on, from rest to 15 m/s
milestones.quality_bar: Boats and barrels as in the sea of Sea of Thieves: they lift as a crest arrives, tilt down its face, and never slide, jitter or lag the water.

items.statement: One dispatch per tick answers every posted point with height, slope, surface velocity and the time derivative of height, valid at the point's use tick, with that tick, the times its layers were made from and a support flag for each layer. For 2,048 points on a gale the long-wave part matches the model at the use tick within 2 mm, and the cascade part matches the model's cascades at the frame's time, carried to the use tick by their rate of change, within M2's bound, with each point's footprint choosing the cascade mip.

At a 60 Hz tick and 120 Hz frames an answer reaches the game one to two ticks after it was asked for, through discarded frames and a stalled readback. An answer used at another tick than its use tick is moved once, by its time derivative, and counted. An answer older than the declared maximum is unavailable and counted, and the blocking-read counter stays at zero.
items.ask: Is there any map, poll or readback in `thrum-sea` or the example that waits for the GPU? Is the counter raised at every place that could?

items.statement: A request over the profile's capacity is refused whole, by body in ID order, counted and shown in the scene's status. A body whose generation changed never receives an answer posted for the old one.

On a glassy sea the craft and the eight floats settle to their hydrostatic drafts and stay there. Through ten minutes of gale, with the craft held at rest, at 5 m/s and at 15 m/s, no body leaves the surface, sinks, capsizes, or gains energy that the waves and its thrust did not give it.

items.statement: A float and the craft rise, pitch and roll with the waves under them: a float lifts as a crest reaches it and tilts down its face, the craft pitches into a head sea and rolls in a beam sea, and nothing slides, jitters or lags the water. milestones.name: The craft leaves a wake that spreads behind it, outlives it, and lifts a float it crosses
milestones.quality_bar: A wake made of water, past the foam trail of the sea of Sea of Thieves: arms and crests that spread at the right angle for the speed, stay where they were made through a turn, travel on after the craft stops, and rock a float in their path.

items.statement: The f64 wake reference in `thrum-sea-model`, forced on deep water by the moving Gaussian pressure patch of `wake_proof.py` (6 m long, 2 m wide), gives a transverse wavelength within 5% of 2πU²/g at 3 m/s and at 6 m/s, a ridge within 3° of 19.47° at 3 m/s and narrower than 19.47° at 6 m/s. After the source is removed a crest travels on at its phase speed.

On Metal the two-level wake follows the reference through a straight run, a turn, a coast and a restart: inside the near window, clear of its border, it differs by under 5% of the field's RMS height. No wave is carried by both levels, and none re-enters a window from its far side.
items.ask: Is the reference a single fine level with the same source, and does the test fail when both levels are given the whole source?

items.statement: A body's wake comes from the vertical force the water put on it, spread over its footprint. The craft at rest on a glassy sea settles to the same draft with the wake on as with it off, and raises no waves once settled. Body records over the profile's source capacity are refused in ID order, counted and shown in the scene's status.

A float 20 m to one side of the craft's track on a glassy sea rises and falls as the wake's crests reach it, at the times the reference gives for its position, and is still again when the wake has passed.

items.statement: On a calm sea the wake reads as water. At 3 m/s two arms spread behind the craft with transverse crests between them; at 12 m/s the wake is narrower; through a turn the old wake stays where it was made and keeps spreading; after the craft stops the waves travel on and fade; a float on the track rocks as they cross.

items.statement: The foam reference in `thrum-sea-model` holds the four stocks and moves material only along the design's transfers. With no birth, aged film gains what fresh film loses, surfacing air becomes fresh film once, aged film rises out of fresh film and fresh film out of submerged air before they fall, the inventory of film and yield-weighted air never rises, and every stock ends at nothing. A birth never takes cover past one.

items.statement: On Metal the foam follows the reference for a scripted set of causes, a patch moves with the drift by the distance the drift gives, and a window shift neither loses nor doubles foam inside the window.

After the craft has passed at 6 m/s and been removed, its trail stays where the water carried it for at least the aged film's lifetime, and is wider and thinner at each later reading.

In a gale, whitecaps form on breaking crests with a bright core and a feathered edge, stay behind the crest as streaks, and fade. A fresh breeze shows fewer and a glassy sea none. milestones.quality_bar: A finished sea: the craft driving through a gale at low Sun, wake and foam behind it, as the sea of Sea of Thieves looks at its best, sharp and stable under MetalFX and smooth on the built-in 120 Hz display.

items.statement: The governor and the MetalFX reconstructor the sea closes on exist: `APPLE-PRESENTATION`'s M7 and M8 are Done.
items.check: python3 -c 'import json,sys; r=json.load(open("docs/plans/APPLE-PRESENTATION/RECORD.json"))["milestones"]; bad=[m for m in ("M7","M8") if not (r.get(m) or {}).get("done")]; print("not Done:", bad); sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)'

items.statement: On the Apple recipe under MetalFX the sea passes M9.6's list, and the five presets pass M9.3's list at noon and low Sun.
items.inspect: M9.6's `realtime` sequences and the stills on the Apple recipe with MetalFX resolved, judged by those lists and against the portable recipe's.

items.statement: The governor lists the sea's knobs and moves each. When the scene is loaded past the refresh it lowers them, and it restores them when the load is gone, with each knob's declared invalidation applied and no query answer changed.

Each Apple-tile variant of a sea kernel that was tried is on record as a paired run against the portable kernel, with the oracle's tolerances checked. One is in use only if its win is beyond the spread of repeated runs.
items.ask: Does `docs/evidence/SEA/M10-recipes.md` give each variant's paired rows and the decision, and does the Apple recipe report which kernels it resolved?

items.statement: At the showcase's extent on both of the Mac's recipes, capture off, in a gale with everything running, the paired cost record is taken for tick frames and for repeat frames, with each sea pass's time beside the sea-absent run. Each tripwire it trips has its investigation beside it. No figure in the record decides this item.
items.ask: Is the extent the one `SHOWCASE`'s Mac rows use, and are both recipes and both frame kinds in the record, with the load on the machine? Does each tripped wire's investigation say what was measured to find the cause, and what was fixed or logged as a follow-up?

items.statement: ATTENDED SETUP: on the built-in display the capture-off release sea scene runs the gale route on both recipes with an OS-reported presented interval for every submission. Each missed refresh is listed and investigated.
items.ask: Does the presented-time witness, as `PLATFORM-RUNTIME-MAC` qualified it, cover the whole route on both recipes with capture off? Is each missed refresh listed with a cause that is fixed, proposed to its owning module, or shown to lie outside the scene?

needs.what: Unlock the Mac, wake the built-in display and keep it awake for one sitting. The agent launches, records and reviews; nothing else is needed. Batch it with any other module's attended items.

items.statement: The whole scene on the Apple recipe reads as a finished sea: the craft at 12 m/s through a gale at low Sun, pitching on the swell, its wake spreading and its foam trailing, the Sun glittering, whitecaps to the horizon.
items.inspect: A `realtime` sequence from a chase view and from 40 m above on the Apple recipe: the hull's waterline, the wake, the trail, the glitter and the horizon.

items.statement: A game maker can add the sea to a scene from the public documentation: the profile, the sea parameters, body records, the query and its mailbox, the limits, counters and knobs.
items.ask: Could a game maker, and the `CLOUDS` planner, use the sea from the documentation and the design alone? Does the documentation say what the sea writes to scene depth and where an effect after it must stop?

items.statement: The maturity ledger's `E1.water` row and `docs/evidence/SEA/PROVENANCE.md` are current: implementation, correctness, visuals and device kept apart, the parked spikes and device runs owed are listed, and every file copied or translated from Broadsides is named with its source commit and path, with the licence of any material that came into Broadsides from elsewhere.
items.ask: Does the ledger claim anything for a device or a recipe that was not run? Does the provenance file match the files in the three packages, and is any listed material GPL or share-alike?

items.statement: Every registered exact baseline, on the Mac and in Chrome, passes the verifier at the claimed commit: this milestone moved no retained image.
